workstreams.name: Per-agent identity principals
workstreams.goal: Replace the single static publish token with scoped, issuable/revocable per-agent principals so every later route, sidecar, and step is built against real identities from day one.
scope_in: Principal model extending accessor/roles.go (coarse: one principal per agent role — e.g. ci-reviewer, platform-mcp, gateway, harvest — with optional ticket/run claim)

Scoped token minting, verification, and revocation replacing the publish-token carve-out in atc/wrappa/api_auth_wrappa.go, with a dual-accept window (static token keeps working behind a deprecation flag)
Migrate the live theborg/cicd agent-review publisher to a scoped principal during the dual-accept window; remove the static token at the end of the window
Per-route scope documentation for every existing and planned /api/v1/agent/* route (the audit later workstreams code against)
Convention for recording the writing principal on agent-authored rows (audit attribution)
scope_out: Per-user human credential vault and Anthropic tokens (credentials-and-budgets)
K8s multi-namespace isolation (spec: out of end-state scope)
The consumers themselves (platform-mcp, gateway, harvest adopt principals when they land)
builds_on: agent/ package publish-token carve-out (the thing being generalized)
workstreams.ships_value: The existing agent-review publisher on theborg authenticates with a scoped, individually-revocable agent principal instead of the shared static token, and every wave-2+ route addition is written against principals once instead of being migrated later.
risks: Must not break the live theborg/cicd review job mid-cutover — dual-accept window with a verified dual-running period is mandatory
Scope taxonomy is defined before all consumers exist; keep it coarse (per-role principal + optional run claim) and extend later
This workstream rewrites the exact auth seam ticket-core and agent-step extend — it is deliberately sequenced a full wave ahead of them

workstreams.name: Credential vault, rate-limit probe, cost ledger, and budget model
workstreams.goal: Vault per-user Anthropic tokens, empirically answer the shared-rate-limit question on theborg before anything is designed around it, land the cost ledger, and be the single owner of all budget arithmetic.
scope_in: agent_user_credentials migration + factory: encrypted at rest reusing Concourse's existing DB encryption-key machinery, expiry timestamps, and a Jira-user-to-platform-user mapping seam column from day one (open item 7 + Jira attribution gap)
fly agent auth walking claude setup-token (headless CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN); expiry-horizon nagging via API field + fly status
Ephemeral K8s secret attach/cleanup helper for runs, including cleanup on abort/error paths (consumed by dispatch and gateway)

FIRST DELIVERABLE: live theborg probe (throwaway namespace, live_*_test.go pattern) — does headless usage share the owner's interactive rate-limit window — with a written decision memo that feeds budget defaults and batch sizing

agent_cost_ledger migration + factory with a NULLABLE ticket FK (no dependency on tickets), fed immediately from the existing agent-review job's ci-agent cost parsing; rollups per ticket/run/user/day + dashboard view; ledger writes are fire-and-forget (never fail a build)

Budget model as the single owner (fixes the orphaned-contract gap): per-ticket budget default (per workflow definition, overridable), global daily cap, and per-step budget-slice arithmetic — how a step's slice derives from the ticket budget and how gateway cutoff and dispatcher admission share it without double-counting — exposed as a Go library (admission check + cutoff config)
Platform-credential policy (fixes the judge/retrospective funding gap): which credential funds platform-initiated LLM work (harvest judge, retrospective agent) and how the ledger attributes it
scope_out: Budget enforcement call-sites (dispatch admission, gateway cutoff consume the library)
Per-repo git deploy credentials (harvest-step owns those)
builds_on: verified claude setup-token findings in spec §11
workstreams.ships_value: fly agent auth vaults a one-year token encrypted at rest with expiry nagging; the existing review job's costs land in agent_cost_ledger attributed per user/day; and the rate-limit question has a written empirical answer before any budget default or batch feature is designed around a guess.
risks: If the probe shows shared rate-limit windows, budget defaults and dispatch concurrency get redesigned — exactly why the probe is the first deliverable, not the last
Encryption-at-rest: reuse of the existing Concourse encryption key seam must be validated early; a new KMS story would balloon scope
The budget-slice arithmetic binds gateway (wave 3) and dispatch (wave 4) — get consumer review on the library API before freezing

workstreams.name: Pipeline runs: one-shot parameterized executions
workstreams.goal: Add run-once lifecycle over instanced pipelines — templates with params schemas, numbered runs, aggregate completion status, retention — as a pure general-CI improvement.
scope_in: template: true pipeline flag (no self-scheduling, resource checks disabled, trigger: true suppressed for run instances, versions pinned at creation) + params schema (names, string/number/bool types, defaults, required) + validator (open item 1)
POST /api/v1/teams/:team/pipelines/:name/runs + fly run-pipeline -p <template> -v k=v; monotonic run numbers as instance_vars {run: N}; entry jobs auto-triggered
pipeline_runs migration + factory (number, params, aggregate status, timestamps)
Run-lifecycle RunnableComponent (polling + notify, never notify-only): worst-of aggregate status, completion detection including in-flight aborts and retriggers (open item 1)
OWNS the parked-run contract (fixes the orphaned-contract gap): a parked agent step counts as running for completion detection — the contract platform-mcp's ask_human rides
Retention (keep_last / ttl) via existing pipeline-archival machinery; template-page runs list (status, params, duration) in the Elm UI
Unit tests on completion/retention + one topgun behavioral spec proving non-template pipelines are untouched
builds_on: Instanced pipelines / instance_vars in core (existing UI/API/fly work unmodified on run instances)
API route recipe (atc/routes.go + atc/api/handler.go + atc/wrappa/api_auth_wrappa.go + accessor/roles.go)
workstreams.ships_value: fly run-pipeline -p regression-suite -v ref=abc launches regression-suite/runs/42, entry jobs fire immediately, the run completes with a queryable worst-of status on the template page, and old runs archive per policy — usable by general CI on theborg before any agent feature exists.
risks: Most invasive core diff in the program: suppressing reactive semantics per-instance must provably not regress live cicd pipelines — the topgun spec is non-negotiable
Completion detection vs aborts/retriggers/late downstream builds is the subtle open item
Params schema creep — hold the line at names/types/defaults/required

workstreams.name: dev-mcp contract, Go client, reference implementation, and sidecar packaging
workstreams.goal: Freeze the five-tool per-repo dev contract, ship a contract-test kit, a code-callable Go client, this repo's own implementation, and the sidecar image packaging convention every later sidecar reuses.
scope_in: Interface finalization (open item 3): tool schemas (list_components, build, run_tests, lint, affected_components), opaque component-id conventions, error taxonomy cleanly separating tests-failed from harness-broke (aligned to the ok/failed/error run taxonomy), streaming/heartbeat semantics for multi-minute test runs
Contract-test kit any repo implementation runs against its server (spec testing approach)
Go client library so platform code (harvest) invokes tools as code, not via an LLM
Reference implementation for this repo mapping components to make/ginkgo targets; second minimal single-component fixture repo to prove layout-agnosticism before freezing

OWNS sidecar image packaging (fixes the unowned-deliverable gap): the build/version/publish convention and CI job for MCP sidecar images, established here and reused verbatim by platform-mcp and gateway
scope_out: Sidecar mounting mechanics inside pods (agent-step proves the wiring)
platform-mcp and gateway tools (their own workstreams)
builds_on: atc/api/mcpserver (protocol.go, server.go, tools.go) as the in-house MCP precedent
CLAUDE.md test-target inventory as reference-impl ground truth
jetbridge sidecar support as the deployment target
workstreams.ships_value: This repo's dev-mcp passes the published contract suite, a Go program drives run_tests(component) end-to-end (the exact call path harvest will use), interactive agents get typed build/test tools today, and the sidecar image packaging convention exists for every later sidecar.
risks: Streaming semantics for long test runs is the hardest design point — a bad choice surfaces as harvest timeouts later (SPDY/exec timeout history in this fork)
Error taxonomy leakage would pollute scorecard metrics downstream
Contract too Concourse-shaped — the second fixture repo is the guard

workstreams.name: Versioned workflow definition store
workstreams.goal: Store, hash, version, import, and promote workflow definitions — the unit of process iteration as data — with the composition grammar decided here and the renderer deliberately excluded.
scope_in: Workflow schema grammar v1 (open item 2): linear ordered step list, prompt packaging (decide inline vs repo-ref for hash stability), model(s), MCP sidecar mix, named checkpoint slots, gate-policy slot, default budget — checkpoint and gate-policy slots are declared-but-inert until their wave-3 consumers land
agent_workflow_definitions migration + factory (name, version, content hash, live flag, config blob) with write-time validation
Content hashing generalized from ci-agent's provenance mechanism
API + fly agent workflows import/list/show/set-live (import from repo files; promotion is a human action, no gate)
Seed library: today's five ci-agent phases decomposed into a v1 definition
scope_out: The renderer (dispatch owns it — definitions resolve to concrete step config at render time; the agent: step never reads these tables)
builds_on: ci-agent phaseconfig/ + phases/ as seed content
workstreams.ships_value: The five-phase ci-agent workflow imports from a repo file as a content-hashed v1, an edited prompt produces a diffable v2, and a human marks it live via fly — workflow iteration becomes versioned data in week one.
risks: The grammar is the highest-leverage schema decision in the platform; constrain v1 to what agent-step and the renderer actually consume
Prompt packaging choice affects both content-hash stability and render-time resolution — decide with dispatch's renderer in mind
Inert slots (checkpoints, gate policy) must be shaped with their wave-3 consumers reviewing the schema before freeze

workstreams.name: Tickets, specs, and plan tasks
workstreams.goal: Land the agent_tickets/agent_ticket_specs/agent_ticket_tasks data model with a single-writer state machine, CRUD API on principals, fly commands, and a minimal web page.
scope_in: Migrations + factories for agent_tickets (full lifecycle enum including all §9 outcome states from day one; origin enum web/fly/jira/retrospective; repo; workflow name+version ref; budget; triggering user), agent_ticket_specs (structured envelope + markdown body), agent_ticket_tasks (id, title, status, ordering, markdown detail)

Single state-transition function in the factory (draft→queued→running→needs-review→outcome states) — the one writer every later component (dispatch, platform-mcp, harvest, outcome watcher) must go through
/api/v1/agent/tickets CRUD routes written against agent principals (identity landed in wave 1) + accessor role entries; fly agent tickets list/create/show
Minimal Elm ticket page: view + edit mode (title, body, budget), lifecycle badge, live task-status list (read side only; PR view comes in delivery-outcomes)
spec.md/plan.md render helper producing read-only workspace input files from DB rows
Open item 10: short Jira-sync phase-2 design note proving the origin + external-ref seam needs no schema redesign
builds_on: web/elm Build/AgentReview.elm as the Elm agent-UI precedent
workstreams.ships_value: A teammate files 'fix X in repo Y' with acceptance criteria on the web UI or via fly, edits the spec body, and tracks lifecycle and task status — usable as the team's agent-work tracker before anything dispatches.
risks: Lifecycle enum must be complete up front (all §9 states) to avoid a follow-up migration
Elm edit-mode scope creep — hold to title/body/budget
The transition function's single-writer discipline is what prevents wave-4 dispatcher/watcher races; design it as the only mutation path now

workstreams.name: Native agent: step with server-side ingestion and sidecar wiring proof
workstreams.goal: Add a first-class agent: step that runs claude in a jetbridge pod with declared MCP sidecars, ingests results/events server-side into agent_run_metrics, proves sidecar-MCP wiring live, and cuts the live theborg review job over.
scope_in: Full step-type recipe: atc/steps.go StepPrecedence + atc/plan.go union + planner + validator + atc/engine/builder.go + atc/exec implementation (copy the fresh run:/sidecar step commits; SidecarSource at atc/steps.go:357)

Step config schema v1: INLINE prompt/config (render-time-resolution rule: this step never reads workflow tables — dispatch's renderer emits this same shape), sidecar mounts, budget-slice env per the credentials-and-budgets arithmetic, artifacts in/out; execution under the resumable jetbridge supervisor with artifacts on the DaemonSet fabric; agent pod holds no push credentials

agent_run_metrics migration + factory; server-side ingestion of results.json + events.ndjson (tokens/turns/wall-time/cost per step) via a principal-authed /api/v1/agent/* ingest route; tolerant of malformed/partial events from crashed agents (record error status, never fail the ingest); ingestion guaranteed to complete before artifact-fabric retention reaps events (fixes the GC-race gap)
Open item 11: extract ONLY the results/events schema types from ci-agent into a shared module both ci-agent and the main module import (not phaserunner)

Live theborg test: agent CLI in the main container calls a stub MCP tool served from a sidecar container — startup ordering, localhost transport in the pause-pod model, teardown (the wiring platform-mcp, gateway, and dev-mcp-as-sidecar all assume)

Cutover of the live theborg/cicd agent-review job (fixes the unowned-migration gap): a hand-written pipeline with an agent: step replaces the build-from-source shell job, with an explicit dual-running verification period
scope_out: Credential vaulting (v1 consumes an ordinary var-source secret; dispatch attaches vaulted creds in wave 4)
The real MCP sidecar servers (dev-mcp, platform-mcp, gateway workstreams)
builds_on: Recent run:/sidecar step commits as the step-type template
atc/worker/jetbridge supervisor (restart-resumable, live_task_resume_test.go), sidecar support (live_sidecar_test.go), DaemonSet artifact fabric
agent-identity principals for the ingest route
workstreams.ships_value: A hand-written pipeline with an agent: step runs claude in a jetbridge pod with sidecars, survives a web-node restart mid-run, lands tokens/turns/cost as queryable rows, passes a live sidecar-MCP wiring test, and the existing theborg review job runs on it dual-verified — the shell scaffolding retired by permanent code.
risks: Widest file surface in the program (validator + planner + engine + exec) — the fresh run: recipe bounds it but expect plan-union edges
Supervisor resume of a mid-conversation agent needs explicit semantics (resume may mean restart-from-checkpoint) — live test required
Sidecar startup ordering (sidecar ready before agent starts) is the unproven wiring being retired here
Schema extraction from ci-agent can snowball — results/events types only

workstreams.name: platform-mcp sidecar with ask_human, checkpoints, and notifications
workstreams.goal: Ship the agent's mid-flight platform surface — read_ticket, submit_spec, submit_plan, update_task_status, ask_human — with park/resume, checkpoint-gate execution, contract tests, and a concrete notification channel.
scope_in: platform-mcp sidecar server (packaged per dev-mcp's image convention) authenticating as a scoped agent principal bound to the ticket/run

Schema-constrained submit_spec/submit_plan/update_task_status writing agent_ticket_specs/agent_ticket_tasks rows through ticket-core's transition/mutation path (structure enters via tool calls, never markdown parsing); read_ticket; live task progress on the ticket page

ask_human(question, options): park the run via jetbridge supervisor wait semantics (pause-pod model), surface question + options on the ticket page, resume on answer; parked step reports as running per pipeline-runs' parked-run contract; per-workflow timeout policy (park / proceed-with-default / fail) read from rendered step config
OWNS checkpoint-gate execution (fixes the ownership hole): workflow-declared checkpoints (e.g. plan approval) execute via the same park/resume primitive

Concrete notification mechanism decision (fixes the undesigned-notification gap): ticket-page banner + one real channel a small team will see (decided against the fork's lossy-NOTIFY lesson — polling-backed)
Contract tests for the platform-mcp interface (spec testing approach requires all three MCP surfaces)
Live theborg test: restart-while-parked — a parked run survives a web-node restart and resumes on answer
scope_out: Terminal mechanics — push/publish/archive are harvest's job (spec litmus test)
Rendering checkpoint declarations into pipelines (dispatch's renderer)
builds_on: agent-step's proven sidecar-MCP wiring and pod model
ticket-core tables/API/transition function and Elm ticket page
workstreams.ships_value: An agent in an agent: step submits spec and plan via typed tools with tasks ticking live on the ticket page; when it calls ask_human the pod parks, the question surfaces with a notification the team actually sees, the run survives a web restart while parked, and resumes the moment a human answers.
risks: Park/resume across web-node restarts is the hard case — fake clientset cannot exercise it; the live test is mandatory
Parked pods consume resources indefinitely — measure pause-pod cost while parked
Notification UX is easy to over-build; one channel plus the banner is v1

workstreams.name: Harvest step: independent re-verification, judge, and push
workstreams.goal: Ship the deterministic platform step that re-runs gates via the dev-mcp Go client against final workspace state, scores with the rubric judge, pushes agent/ticket-N with harvest-only credentials, and updates the ticket with evidence.
scope_in: Harvest step type reusing agent-step's plan/engine plumbing (non-LLM control path); terminal-step config schema published early in the wave (dispatch's renderer consumes it next wave)

Gate policy language v1 (open item 4): named check list, affected_components-first then full suite per policy, an explicit flake/retry stance from day one — declared in the workflow definition's gate-policy slot, interpreted here; gates invoked as code through the dev-mcp Go client

Rubric judge (open item 5): schema-constrained verdict scoring (atium's method, reusing ci-agent scoring machinery); rubric format and its mapping to the six-verdict feedback taxonomy agreed with delivery-outcomes and scorecards before either UI lands; judge funded per credentials-and-budgets' platform-credential policy
Push agent/ticket-<n> using per-repo git credentials mounted ONLY into the harvest pod; live theborg security test that agent pods can never see them; patch manifest + review-evidence links
Extend agent_reviews/agent_feedback with ticket/run linkage columns (fixes the extended-not-duplicated gap) so evidence publishes against tickets, not just repo/commit
Ticket update through the transition function on every outcome: gates pass → push + needs-review with evidence; gates fail → needs-review with failing evidence, nothing pushed
Fixture-workspace test suite: gates pass / fail / flaky (spec testing approach)
scope_out: Diff/PR rendering on the ticket page (delivery-outcomes)
builds_on: dev-mcp Go client + contract + error taxonomy
agent-step engine/exec plumbing and jetbridge pod execution
ci-agent scoring/provenance machinery for the judge
workstreams.ships_value: Given a workspace with committed work (fixture or agent: step output), harvest independently re-runs build+tests through the repo's dev-mcp, runs the funded rubric judge, pushes agent/ticket-7 with credentials only it holds, and flips the ticket to needs-review with gate evidence and score — verify-state-not-transcripts real, and the §5 credential posture closed in wave 3.
risks: Flaky gates make independent re-verification cry wolf — the fixture suite's flaky case and the retry stance are the trust foundation of the whole platform
Long full-suite runs push against step timeouts — leans directly on dev-mcp's streaming semantics
The rubric-to-six-verdict mapping is a three-party agreement (harvest, delivery-outcomes, scorecards) — get sign-off before freezing

workstreams.name: agent-gateway-mcp: provider-agnostic subagents with metering and cutoff
workstreams.goal: Ship the gateway sidecar exposing request_review and ask_agent over an adapter layer, metering every cross-agent call into the flight recorder and cost ledger, with budget-slice cutoff that never silently truncates.
scope_in: Gateway sidecar (built via dev-mcp's packaging convention) with request_review(diff, rubric) and ask_agent(prompt, provider, model) tool schemas + contract tests

Adapter layer with v1 in-sidecar execution: claude CLI adapter first (reusing ci-agent invocation + cost parsing), adapter interface ready for codex/cursor-cli and a future platform-scheduled-pod backend behind the same contract

Universal metering: tokens/turns/cost/latency per call emitted in the shared events.ndjson schema (flight recorder) and written fire-and-forget to agent_cost_ledger; cost normalization at the adapter boundary
Budget-slice cutoff per the credentials-and-budgets library: halt with a partial-work-product signal surfacing as needs-review, never silent truncation — tested explicitly
Sidecar authenticates as a scoped agent principal; provider calls use the run-attached user credential (or platform credential per policy)
scope_out: Judge execution (harvest invokes the judge directly)
builds_on: ci-agent adapter/ + llm/ claude-CLI invocation and cost parsing
agent-step's proven sidecar wiring, budget-slice env, and shared events schema
credentials-and-budgets budget library + ledger + ephemeral credential
workstreams.ships_value: An agent (or a plain test harness) calls request_review through the gateway and gets a rubric-structured review back; the call's tokens/cost/latency land in the flight recorder and ledger; and a deliberately tiny budget slice demonstrably halts the call with a clean, non-silent cutoff signal.
risks: Bundling provider CLIs makes a fat, churny image — pin versions, ship one provider at GA, automate rebuilds via the packaging pipeline
Non-claude adapters may only meter turns/latency at first — label partial metering so scorecards don't lie
Cutoff-mid-conversation semantics (partial result vs hard fail) must match the never-silent-truncation rule and be tested

workstreams.name: Workflow renderer + dispatcher: queued ticket to funded pipeline run
workstreams.goal: Render workflow-definition versions into concrete pipeline templates (golden-file validated), then ship the RunnableComponent that claims queued tickets, admits against budgets, attaches vaulted credentials, and makes 'queued' sufficient.
scope_in: MILESTONE 1 — renderer library: workflow definition version → template: true pipeline config with fully-resolved agent: step config (render-time-resolution rule — steps never read workflow tables), sidecar mix, gate policy, checkpoint declarations, and the terminal harvest step; golden-file tests per definition version validated against atc configvalidate; rendered spec.md/plan.md materialized as run inputs; hand-dispatch via fly run-pipeline supported immediately (retires the wave-3 hand-written template)

MILESTONE 2 — dispatcher RunnableComponent (atc/component.go constant + atccmd/command.go wiring, polling + notify, never notify-only): SQL claim/retry/timeout semantics with attempt caps under multi-web-node deployments
Budget admission via the credentials-and-budgets library (per-ticket + global daily cap); over-cap dispatches stay queued, never failed; platform faults produce error, not failed
Credential resolution from agent_user_credentials → ephemeral K8s secret attached to the run's pods; credential-expiry mid-run → error with owner noted
Ticket state transitions (queued→running→needs-review/failed/error) exclusively through ticket-core's transition function (single-writer discipline)
scope_out: Experiment batch creation (process-intel-experiments reuses this renderer)
builds_on: registrar/reaper RunnableComponent pattern + polling-not-notify-only fork lesson
agent-step config schema (frozen wave 2) + harvest terminal-step schema (frozen wave 3)
credentials-and-budgets vault, secret helper, and budget library
workstreams.ships_value: Setting a ticket to queued is the whole human action: the dispatcher claims it, checks budgets, attaches the filer's vaulted token, renders the live workflow version into a numbered pipeline run whose agent: steps and harvest step execute in jetbridge pods, and walks the ticket to needs-review — the manual fly dispatch retired.
risks: The renderer is the integration point of four frozen schemas — golden-file tests per definition version are the honesty mechanism
Claim semantics under concurrent web nodes need SQL-level care (follow existing GC-collector claiming)
State-machine races with platform-mcp/harvest/watcher writes — mitigated only if everyone goes through the single transition function

workstreams.name: Ticket PR view, dispositions, and outcome watcher
workstreams.goal: Turn the ticket page into a lightweight PR view and ship the native outcome watcher that records merged / merged-with-fixes / human-touch delta without webhooks.
scope_in: Elm ticket PR view: diff of agent/ticket-N vs base (paginated/limited for large branches), review-evidence panel reusing Build/AgentReview.elm machinery, judge score, plan-task progress, cost from ledger rollups, six-verdict finding feedback
Ticket-level disposition UI: sent-back / abandoned with a small reason taxonomy + free text
agent_outcomes migration + factory (merge state, human-touch delta, disposition + reason) — the nullable-join schema agreed with scorecards at wave start

Outcome watcher RunnableComponent (open item 8): polling cadence with polite configurable rate, branch-head-reachable-from-default for merged, pre-merge human-commit detection for merged-with-fixes, human-touch delta (lines changed post-agent) with a patch-id fallback for squash merges and documented v1 heuristic limits — native repo checking, no webhooks
Outcome states flow into the ticket lifecycle exclusively via the transition function
scope_out: Jira status sync (phase 2, rides the origin seam)
builds_on: harvest-step's branch convention, patch manifest, judge score, and agent_reviews ticket/run linkage
RunnableComponent recipe + existing git repo-checking machinery
credentials-and-budgets ledger rollups for cost display
workstreams.ships_value: A completed ticket's page shows diff, proof-carrying evidence, judge score, plan progress, and cost; when the branch merges upstream the watcher flips the ticket to merged — or merged-with-fixes with the exact human-touch delta recorded — the platform's most honest quality metric accumulating with no webhook and no form.
risks: Human-touch delta under rebases/squash merges is genuinely hard — v1 is best-effort with merge-strategy assumptions documented
Large-diff Elm rendering needs limits to avoid a heavy UI
Delta definition (lines vs hunks) must be fixed before scorecards consume it — part of the wave-start schema agreement

workstreams.name: Workflow scorecards and run metrics surfaces
workstreams.goal: Compare workflow-definition versions side-by-side on objective and subjective metrics, and answer 'where did the turns go' for any run.
scope_in: Scorecard rollup queries + API + Elm view over agent_run_metrics / agent_cost_ledger / judge scores / gate results keyed by workflow-definition version: gate pass rate, cost per ticket, turns, findings per ticket, judge scores, human verdict distributions — with counts alongside rates (small-team sample honesty)

Outcome-derived columns (merge rate, merged-untouched, sent-back, time-to-merge, human-touch delta) via NULLABLE joins onto agent_outcomes, filling as the same-wave watcher lands (schema agreed at wave start)
Run/ticket page per-step metrics panel ('where did the turns go'), including gateway cross-provider call metering
ok/failed/error taxonomy enforced end-to-end in every rollup (agent-did-badly vs platform-broke)
Indexes by (workflow_version, day) from day one
scope_out: Promotion gates (none, ever — scorecards inform, humans decide)
builds_on: agent_run_metrics + shared events schema from agent-step
harvest-step gate results + judge scores + verdict mapping
workstreams.ships_value: Two live-candidate workflow versions display side-by-side scorecards (gate pass rate, cost, turns, judge scores, verdict distributions) over real runs, and any run's page shows exactly where its turns and dollars went — promotion decisions get data.
risks: Outcome columns land dark until the same-wave watcher fills them — nullable-by-design keeps neither workstream blocking the other
Small-team sample sizes make scorecards noisy — present counts, resist overreading
Metric definitions must match the harvest/delivery-outcomes agreements or the scorecard lies

workstreams.name: Experiments, benchmarks, and process intelligence
workstreams.goal: Close the loop: opt-in benchmark experiments across workflow versions, finding analytics, calibration, friction mining, and a retrospective agent that files origin:retrospective tickets proposing concrete process changes.
scope_in: MILESTONE 1 — experiments: benchmark case storage decision (in-repo dir vs DB) + agent_benchmark_cases/agent_experiments migrations as needed (open item 6); extraction-skill port mining {ticket prompt, beforeRef, referenceRef} from team repos; experiment runner creating a batch of pipeline runs across definition variants via dispatch's renderer + pipeline-runs API, under the global daily cap, producing a scorecard delta view

MILESTONE 2 — intelligence: finding analytics (agent_reviews findings per repo and workflow version; recurring classes as automation candidates; catches-migrate-leftward metric — findings per ticket trending down while escaped defects stay flat); calibration (false-positive rate from six-verdict feedback; missed-issue rate via a lightweight defect→ticket linking convention, agreed before data accrues); friction mining limited to 2-3 high-signal flight-recorder signatures (failing-test loops, tool-error rates)

Retrospective workflow v1 (open item 9): manual-triggered cadence first, then recurring; an agent: step run reading findings/verdicts/friction/outcomes and filing origin:retrospective tickets with template-shaped proposals (lint rule, prompt amendment, dev-mcp gate, workflow edit) into the normal human-merged loop; funded per the platform-credential policy
Analytics API + minimal Elm views
scope_out: Auto-applying process changes (proposals are tickets; main stays human-gated)
New metric ingestion pipelines (reads existing tables only)
builds_on: agent_reviews + agent_feedback (extended in harvest-step, not duplicated)
forge cgx.md friction-notes practice being mechanized
workstreams.ships_value: fly agent experiments run executes a 5-case benchmark across two workflow versions and prints the scorecard delta; a retrospective run reads a month of findings, friction, and merge outcomes and files a concrete improvement ticket ('add lint rule X — caught 4 times in review') into the same queue the team already works — the platform improving itself on theborg.
risks: Deliberately the widest terminal workstream (kept single to stay within the 14-track cap) — the two milestones are internally sequenced and separately shippable; split into two forge tracks at execution time if needed
Retrospective proposal quality is unproven — template-shaped proposals and manual triggering first
Friction signatures need run volume to mean anything — ship the queries, expect tuning
Experiment batches multiply spend — the daily cap is load-bearing here

scaffolding_decisions: REJECTED B's glue-dispatch workstream (shell agent task + shell harvest + static-token platform writes). The judges' fatal findings stand: it orphans the renderer, its ask_human/park '~zero rework' claim breaks down for parking semantics, it keeps agent and push credentials co-resident for ~3 waves, and it forces the flight-recorder ingestion path to be written twice. The early end-to-end demo it bought is achieved instead with permanent pieces (next item).

ACCEPTED (bounded, config-only scaffolding): at the end of wave 3, a HAND-WRITTEN template: true pipeline containing real agent: steps and the real harvest step, dispatched manually via fly run-pipeline -v ticket_id=N. This closes the full ticket→agent→verified-pushed-branch loop one wave before the dispatcher, using zero throwaway code — the only artifact retired is one pipeline YAML, replaced by dispatch's renderer in wave 4.

ACCEPTED: dual-accept window for the static publish token during agent-identity's wave-1 cutover, so the live theborg/cicd review job never breaks; the static token is deleted at window end. All later routes are written against principals from day one (rejecting B's build-on-static-token-then-migrate).

ACCEPTED: agent-step (wave 2) consumes its Anthropic token from an ordinary var-source/K8s secret until dispatch attaches vaulted per-user credentials in wave 4. This is pipeline-config-level scaffolding only — no code changes when the vaulted path takes over.

ACCEPTED: workflow-store's checkpoint and gate-policy grammar slots are declared-but-inert in wave 1, with their wave-3 consumers (platform-mcp, harvest) reviewing the slot shapes before the grammar freezes — avoiding both grammar over-design and a later breaking schema change.

ACCEPTED: scorecards' outcome-derived columns are nullable joins designed at wave-4 start with delivery-outcomes; they render dark until the same-wave watcher fills them. Neither workstream blocks the other.

REJECTED judge-3's stub-harvest renderer variant: because the renderer lives in dispatch (wave 4) and harvest's terminal-step schema freezes in wave 3, the renderer targets a real, frozen schema and no stub is ever built. The C-style wave-2 renderer↔harvest knot is dissolved by sequencing, not by a placeholder.

REJECTED double ingestion (B's artifact-triggered flight recorder followed by native ingest): server-side ingestion is built once, inside agent-step, in wave 2 — meeting spec §5's 'ingest server-side, not just as artifacts' from the first native run.

ACCEPTED: process-intel-experiments is deliberately one wide terminal workstream (to respect the 14-track cap) with two internally-sequenced, separately-shippable milestones (experiments/benchmarks, then intelligence/retrospective); split into two forge tracks at execution time if it proves too large.
synthesis_notes:
Base and structure. The synthesis takes proposal C's dependency discipline as the skeleton (per judges 1 and 3: verified file citations, named owners for the renderer, checkpoint gates, and the vault/probe) but re-cuts its infeasible six-stream wave 1 into a 5/2/3/3/1 shape that resolves the auth-switch contention structurally: agent-identity lands in wave 1 alongside four streams that never touch api_auth_wrappa.go (credentials, pipeline-runs, dev-mcp, workflow-store), and the two streams that extend the auth switch (ticket-core, agent-step) move to wave 2 with declared dependencies on identity — turning judge 3's 'wave 1a' hack into real wave ordering.

Grafts. (1) A's render-time-resolution rule is adopted verbatim and recorded as a contract surface: the agent: step never reads workflow tables; dispatch's renderer resolves definition refs into the same inline config shape hand-written pipelines use. (2) A's single-owner budget/ledger is merged with C's zero-dependency vault+probe into one wave-1 governance stream (credentials-and-budgets), fixing A's false ticket-core dependency via a nullable ledger FK and making one workstream the owner of ALL budget arithmetic — including the previously orphaned per-step budget-slice semantics. (3) C's two signature risk-retirement moves are kept and placed: the theborg rate-limit probe is the FIRST deliverable of credentials-and-budgets (wave 1), and the live sidecar-MCP wiring proof is an explicit deliverable of agent-step (wave 2), before the three sidecar workstreams that assume the wiring. (4) B's early-value insight is honored without its glue: the loop closes at end of wave 3 via a hand-written template + manual fly run-pipeline using only permanent pieces (see scaffolding decisions), roughly matching B's demo timing while avoiding its renderer orphan, credential co-residency, and double-ingestion costs.

Judge-found dependency errors, all fixed: renderer has a single owner (dispatch, milestone 1) consuming schemas frozen in prior waves — no A-style hidden intra-wave dep and no C-style wave-2 knot; checkpoint-gate execution is owned by platform-mcp-hitl using the ask_human park/resume primitive; the judge's credential/funding story is owned by credentials-and-budgets' platform-credential policy, which harvest declares as a dependency; experiments moved behind dispatch (wave 5), killing A's scorecards→renderer same-wave hazard; harvest declares workflow-store (gate-policy slot) and credentials-and-budgets; gateway declares credentials-and-budgets (vault + budget library) and agent-step (events schema, wiring); the parked-run-counts-as-running contract is owned by pipeline-runs with platform-mcp as consumer; the ingest route rides principals landed a wave earlier.

Judge-found spec gaps, all assigned: platform-initiated LLM funding → credentials-and-budgets; budget-slice arithmetic → credentials-and-budgets (single owner); live theborg review-job cutover with a dual-running period → agent-step (native step migration) + agent-identity (principal cutover); ask_human notification channel decision → platform-mcp-hitl; platform-mcp contract tests → platform-mcp-hitl; sidecar image build/publish convention → dev-mcp; agent_reviews/agent_feedback ticket/run linkage (extend-not-duplicate) → harvest-step; flight-recorder ingestion-before-artifact-GC guarantee → agent-step; Jira-user mapping seam column → credentials-and-budgets (with ticket-core's origin design note).

Coverage. Spec sections: §1 ticket-core; §2 workflow-store (+renderer in dispatch); §3 pipeline-runs; §4 dispatch; §5 agent-step + harvest-step; §6 dev-mcp + platform-mcp-hitl + gateway-mcp; §7 harvest-step + delivery-outcomes; §8 agent-step (ingestion) + scorecards + harvest-step (judge) + process-intel-experiments (experiments); §9 delivery-outcomes; §10 platform-mcp-hitl (HITL/checkpoints) + process-intel-experiments; §11 credentials-and-budgets + agent-identity. Open items: 1→pipeline-runs, 2→workflow-store, 3→dev-mcp, 4→harvest-step, 5→harvest-step (mapping co-signed by delivery-outcomes and scorecards), 6→process-intel-experiments, 7→credentials-and-budgets, 8→delivery-outcomes, 9→process-intel-experiments, 10→ticket-core, 11→agent-step (results/events extraction only; workflow-store reuses ci-agent provenance hashing by import, no extraction).

Value cadence per wave: W1 — general-CI pipeline runs on theborg, vaulted tokens + cost ledger fed by the existing review job, typed dev-mcp tools for interactive agents, versioned workflow definitions, revocable agent principals. W2 — team ticket tracker; the live review job on a restart-surviving native agent: step with queryable metrics. W3 — full loop demo (hand-dispatched): agent implements a ticket with ask_human available, harvest independently verifies, judges, and pushes with isolated credentials. W4 — 'queued' is sufficient; PR view + automatic merge outcomes; version scorecards. W5 — experiments and the self-improving retrospective loop.
